details.voting_rule: Each field is judged on 3 independent runs. It is a conflict only if at least 2 runs say conflict, a match only if at least 2 runs say match, and unknown otherwise. The score counts voted conflicts: 0, 1, 2, 3 or more give 95, 60, 35, 10.

plain_finding.what_we_found: We checked your starting price, free trial, product category and target customer on your site against independent review sites for Close, and they match on every point.
plain_finding.what_it_costs_you: Nothing is broken here, so no customer is being lost to a competitor over mismatched facts today.
plain_finding.fix_it_today: Keep a simple monthly check of those four facts on your site and on the review sites, and correct any listing the moment it drifts.

details.method_note: Check weights are our own judgment. AI crawler access, structured data, and heading structure come from GEO-16 (Kumar and Palkhouski, 2025). The static content check comes from Vercel and MERJ's December 2024 research, which found GPTBot and ClaudeBot only fetch raw HTML and never execute JavaScript, so content that only appears after a client-side render is invisible to them even though a human visitor sees it fine.

plain_finding.what_we_found: AI search tools can reach your homepage, but they only read the raw text before any scripts run. That raw text is 407 words, so much of what a customer sees on screen may not be read at all.
plain_finding.what_it_costs_you: When a customer asks an AI search tool about your product, it answers from that thin text, so it may describe you poorly or point the customer to a competitor.
plain_finding.fix_it_today: Open your homepage with scripts turned off in your browser and check that the main headline, product description, and pricing text are all visible in plain text.

conclusion: For these questions, AI mostly reads 'best tools' lists and comparisons written by other companies, and only 26% of them mention you.
